2: Why keep a dashboard as a file?
Because a workbook edited in the portal is a change nobody reviewed, and an export of it can carry the subscription, resource group and workspace into a repository.

By the end of this chapter you can rebuild the workbook's template from reviewed files, prove it has one tab per daily check and no embedded I D's, and catch the portal edits that would otherwise drift into production unreviewed.
It's for the developers and for the security operations engineer who edits the workbook.
3: Here's what Microsoft Learn gives you.
Two ways to manage a workbook as a template: copy the Gallery Template from the Advanced Editor, or copy the Resource Manager template.
The instance is a Microsoft dot Insights workbooks resource, kind shared, with a display name, a source I D, a category, and serialized data, which holds the workbook's content.
And Learn warns that an exported template often embeds the subscription I D and resource group: its advice is to mask them.
The resource reference gives A P I version 2023-06-01.
Queries use the Logs data source, with K Q L.
4: What does it leave to you?

Learn's way is to export from the portal and paste, so the template is whatever someone last saved; the kit builds it from the manifest and the K Q L files, and a test keeps the committed file equal to the build.
Masking I D's by hand misses one sooner or later, so a check fails any G U I D, subscription path, address or secret.
A query is free text, so the kit checks each tab's tables and each query's look-back.
It checks that every query reads the workspace parameter.
And because nothing says what a tab means, every tab must carry the banner.
5: The template has a header with the banner, then the parameters: a workspace picker and four text values, all left empty in the template.

Then one tab per daily check, and one group per tab that shows when its tab is selected, holding the banner, the daily check, what to do, the link-outs with click paths, the G C C note, and its queries, each one a Logs query on the workspace parameter.
The validator runs ten checks: the format, one tab per check, tables, look-backs, the workspace, the banner, link-outs and hosts, queries per tab kind, the telemetry list, and no I D's or secrets.

A copy was exported after someone edited the workbook in the portal.

Four edits, four failures: one risk query reads a workspace path instead of the parameter; the devices query looks back seven hundred and twenty hours; the grants tab lost its banner; and the file carries a G U I D and a subscription path.
Step 4 shows what the export carried: the workspace's full resource path, exactly what Microsoft Learn says to mask.

10: Lab 2 runs in a test subscription, never production, and the authors haven't run it.
Open the template in the portal through the Advanced Editor, pick the test workspace, and open all ten tabs.
Save a test copy, change one look-back, and copy the Gallery Template back out.
Validate the export: your edit fails, and so does the workspace the portal saved into it.
Record any other difference the portal introduced; that confirms the item format, which Learn doesn't document field by field.
Then delete the test copy and the export.
